sections.heading: The gerund as a clause
sections.body:
A gerund at the start of a sentence can stand for a whole clause. Context tells you the meaning:

- **Manner / means**: *Estudiando mucho, aprobó.* (By studying a lot…)
- **Cause**: *Siendo tan tarde, decidimos quedarnos.* (Since it was so late…)
- **Condition**: *Saliendo ahora, llegamos a tiempo.* (If we leave now…)
- **Concession** (with *aun*): *Aun teniendo dinero, vive con muy poco.* (Even though he has money…)
- **Time**: *Caminando por el parque, vi a Marta.* (While walking…)

The gerund should be simultaneous with or before the main verb. "Gerund of consequence" or of a later event is considered an error in formal writing: ✗ *Chocó, muriendo al instante* — prefer *Chocó y murió al instante.*

sections.heading: Absolute participle clauses
sections.body:
A participle with its own subject, placed first, expresses something completed before the main action. It agrees with its noun:

*Terminada la cena, salimos a caminar.* (Once dinner was over, we went for a walk.)
*Dicho esto, se fue.* (Having said this, he left.)
*Firmado el contrato, empezaron las obras.* (Once the contract was signed, work began.)
*Resueltos los problemas, todo fue más fácil.*

They're formal but also common in speech: *Dicho y hecho.* (No sooner said than done.)

sections.heading: Participle vs. adjective
sections.body: A few verbs have a regular participle (for perfect tenses) and a short adjective form: *despertado / despierto* (*He despertado a Juan* vs. *Juan está despierto*), *soltado / suelto* (loose), *imprimido / impreso* (both acceptable as participles in LatAm: *He impreso / he imprimido el documento*), *freído / frito*.

examples: Estudiando mucho, aprobó el examen.
By studying a lot, she passed the exam.
Siendo tan tarde, decidimos quedarnos.
Since it was so late, we decided to stay.
Saliendo ahora, llegamos a tiempo.
If we leave now, we'll arrive on time.
Aun teniendo dinero, vive con muy poco.
Even though he has money, he lives on very little.
Caminando por el parque, vi a Marta.
While walking through the park, I saw Marta.
Chocó y murió al instante.
He crashed and died instantly.
Terminada la cena, salimos a caminar.
Once dinner was over, we went for a walk.
Dicho esto, se fue.
Having said this, he left.
Firmado el contrato, empezaron las obras.
Once the contract was signed, the work began.
Resueltos los problemas, todo fue más fácil.
With the problems solved, everything was easier.
Dicho y hecho.
No sooner said than done.
Juan ya está despierto.
Juan is already awake.
El perro anda suelto.
The dog is on the loose.
¿Ya tienes impreso el documento?
Do you already have the document printed?
Me encanta el pescado frito.
I love fried fish.
